title: How to Resize a Photo for an Online Form
description: A checklist for matching an online form's photo dimensions, file-size ceiling, aspect ratio and format without stretching the image.
intro: Online forms may specify a photo's pixel dimensions, maximum file size, aspect ratio, format and background. Meeting one requirement does not automatically satisfy the others, so check the form's latest instructions before exporting.

sections.heading: Copy the form's exact requirements
paragraphs: Note the required width and height, maximum KB or MB, accepted formats and any rules about background, crop, colour or file naming. Application requirements can change; do not rely on an old screenshot or a different organization's form.
If the form states an aspect ratio, use it to guide the crop. Keep the subject positioned as required and leave enough of the image around the edges for the destination's crop behavior.

sections.heading: Crop and resize without distortion
paragraphs: Crop to the required shape before changing dimensions when the source ratio differs. Keep proportions locked while resizing so the photo is not stretched. Upscaling a small image cannot restore detail that was not captured.

Use the Crop Image tool to select the area to keep, then the Image Resizer to set pixel dimensions. A form-specific workflow may exist—for example, the DSSSB Photo Resizer targets its named use case; it is not a universal form preset.

sections.heading: Meet the file-size limit
paragraphs: After dimensions and crop are correct, choose an accepted file format. JPEG is common for photographs, but always follow the form's allowed types. Use the Image Compressor or Image Resizer in KB to reduce bytes while checking that facial details remain clear.
Leave a margin below the maximum if possible. Some portals interpret size units differently or re-encode images after upload.

sections.heading: Verify before submitting
paragraphs: Open the exported image and confirm dimensions, format, file size, crop, background and visual clarity. Then follow the form's own preview or validation messages. Keep the original photo separate from the upload copy.
If the portal rejects a file that appears to meet the numbers, check for hidden requirements such as colour mode, naming convention, maximum dimensions or a stricter size threshold.

faq.question: Can I use one exact photo size for every form?
faq.answer: No. Different forms specify different dimensions, formats, crops and file-size limits. Follow the current destination's instructions.

faq.question: Should I crop or resize first?
faq.answer: If the target aspect ratio differs, crop intentionally first; then resize to the required pixel dimensions while preserving proportions.

faq.question: Why does the form reject my correctly sized photo?
faq.answer: It may also validate format, file size, aspect ratio, colour mode, background or naming. Check the complete specification and error message.

faq.question: Will making a photo larger improve its quality?
faq.answer: No. Upscaling adds pixels but cannot recreate detail missing from the original capture.
